# Hiring Without Whiteboards

A list of companies (or teams) that don't do "whiteboard" interviews. "Whiteboards" are used as a metaphor, and are a _symbol_ for the kinds of CS trivia questions that are associated with bad interview practices. Whiteboards are not bad – CS trivia questions are. Using sites like HackerRank/LeetCode _probably_ fall into a similar category.

The companies and teams listed here use interview techniques and questions that resemble day-to-day work. For example, pairing on a real world problem or a paid/unpaid take home exercise. Read (and contribute to) [our recommendations](RECOMMENDATIONS.md) for ways to conduct better interviews.

### tl;dr

- Discussing a real world problem (with or without whiteboard) is 👍
- Solving CS trivia, technical puzzles, riddles, brainteasers (with or without whiteboard) is 👎

Please open a [PR](https://github.com/poteto/hiring-without-whiteboards/pull/new/master) to be added.

### Duds

If you've been through an interview with one of these companies recently, and your experience suggests otherwise from their description, please open a [PR](https://github.com/poteto/hiring-without-whiteboards/pull/new/master) to remove them from this list.

Cat Burglar plugs a real browser into your agent. It can run patched stealth Chromium, stock Chromium for devtools, or Obscura's 43 MB Rust engine behind one session. It sends diffs instead of full DOM dumps, remembers per-site workflows, and gates high-impact actions. | **Site memory** | Per-origin hints and workflows learned after a successful run. Repeated tasks get shorter. |

| **Remote CDP and cloud** | Attach to Browserbase, Steel, Browserless, Obscura Cloud, or a local logged-in Chrome. No local browser process. |
| **Deep DevTools on demand** | HAR, CPU profiles, heap snapshots, coverage, and network/CPU throttling, captured only while you ask. |

# Tag-per-Track MCP Server

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/tag-per-track-mcp.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/tag-per-track-mcp)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

This project is a local **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** server that allows AI agents (like Claude) to analyze audio files via the **Tag-per-Track** API. It authenticates either with a **Studio API key** (prepaid credits bought on [tag-per-track.cloud](https://tag-per-track.cloud), no crypto needed) or with a wallet, in which case it automatically handles the USDC micro-payment using the **x402** protocol on the **Base** network.

## 🎯 Vision
Enable an AI to "pay to listen" autonomously. When an AI agent wants to analyze a track, it uses this MCP server, which signs an EIP-3009 (USDC) payment authorization and instantly retrieves the enriched track metadata.

## 🚀 Features
- **`analyze_audio` Tool (Canonical)**: Extracts BPM, Genre, Mood, Key, Instruments, production metrics, optional Lyrics (1 credit or 0.15 USDC standard / 2 credits or 0.25 USDC with lyrics), **AI-Generated Music Detection** (`ai_detection`: Suno, Udio, neural vocoders with `HUMAN`, `AI_GENERATED`, or `UNCERTAIN` verdicts) and the server-side **A&R evaluation** (`arEvaluation`: discovery / signing / beatmaker profiles).
- **`analyze_audio_with_lyrics` Tool (Alias)**: Extracts complete musical metadata, transcribes full vocal lyrics, and returns AI origin integrity metrics (2 credits or 0.25 USDC).
- **`analyze_audio_batch` Tool (Parallel Processing)**: Analyzes multiple music tracks concurrently with AI origin detection on every track, dramatically reducing turnaround time for albums and playlists.
- **`triage_demo_folder` Tool (Demo Inbox Triage)**: Sorts a whole local folder of demos in one call: analysis, artist/title from `Artist - Title` file names or audio tags, Spotify traction, A&R scoring v2 re-computed with the traction, and a compact ranked report with buckets (`priority`, `listen`, `pass`, `ai_flagged`, `error`). Unreliable lyrics (instrumental, no voice, looping hallucination) are flagged instead of quoted.
- **`lookup_artist_stats` Tool (A&R Traction)**: Fetches public Spotify streaming traction (monthly listeners, followers, popularity score, genres) for hybrid A&R qualification.

DataRanger patrols your data, fixes what it can prove, and calls you for the rest.

A park ranger walks the trails, fixes what is safe to fix on the spot, radios in anything dangerous, and files a report. DataRanger does the same for your tables. It finds data-quality incidents, tests every candidate fix on a copy against the source's control totals, applies only the fixes it can prove, and keeps wrong fixes under a rate you choose. Everything else goes to a person, with the evidence attached.

The dotted line under the name is a patrol trail: one marker per daily partition, the same marks the patrol console uses.

--- Most data-quality tools stop at an alert. Letting an AI agent fix data is the obvious next step, and a risky one: a wrong fix can pass every monitor you have. In the DQ-Repair benchmark, a rules engine left wrong data behind in 31% of incidents and an agent checked only by monitors in 24%. candidates.readme_excerpt:
<!-- mcp-name: io.github.AIops-tools/cicd-aiops -->

# CICD AIops

> **Audit availability:** Real writes require a committed `pending` audit row and stop before contacting the platform if storage is unavailable. Reads and previews may continue with a warning; new audit rows store outcome summaries rather than full responses.

**Governed AI-ops for self-managed GitLab and self-hosted Gitea.**

`cicd-aiops` is for the team running its *own* CI/CD forge — a GitLab instance
or a Gitea server on your hardware, in your lab, behind your VPN — who want an
AI agent that can answer "why did the pipeline fail?", "which runner is
wedged?", "where did 40 GB of artifact storage go?" and "what work went
stale?" and then act (retry, cancel, pause, delete, protect) **only** through
an audited, budgeted, risk-tiered, undo-recorded governance harness. It is not
a SaaS integration: it speaks the GitLab REST API v4 and the Gitea API v1
directly against your server, with credentials encrypted at rest.

> **Verification status**: modelled from each project's public API docs and
> exercised against mocked HTTP responses; there is no recorded end-to-end run
> against a live server yet. `cicd-aiops doctor` is the fastest live check —
> see [`docs/VERIFICATION.md`](docs/VERIFICATION.md).

> **Routing**: Do NOT use this for Kubernetes deploy state — use k8s-aiops.
> This tool ends at the CI/CD server's API (pipelines, runners, artifacts,
> repo hygiene).

## What this tool does, and does not, decide

It delivers CI/CD operations — reads and writes — accurately and efficiently, and
records every one of them. It does **not** decide whether a write is allowed to
happen. That is the agent's judgement, or the permission of the token you connect
it with: give it a GitLab/Gitea access token without write scope and the writes
fail at the server — the place that actually owns the permission.

So there is no read-only switch, no policy file, no approval gate to configure.
The one thing the tool guarantees is that nothing is silent: **every call, over
MCP and over the CLI alike, lands an audit row** in `~/.cicd-aiops/audit.db`,
and destructive writes still capture their before-state and record an inverse
where one exists.

> Each tool declares a `risk_level`, kept in agreement with its `[READ]`/`[WRITE]`
> documentation tag by a test, and carried into the audit row as a descriptive
> tier — so a reviewer can see at a glance that a row was a high-risk delete. It
> is a label, not a gate.

candidates.description: Turn webhooks into MCP Events for AI agents, with the hosted Hookdeck Event Gateway receiving and delivering them. Sources include Resend, GitHub, Stripe, Slack and any signed webhook. Poll tools and a Claude Code plugin cover clients without MCP Events support.
candidates.readme_excerpt: # MCP Events bridge Turn webhooks into [MCP Events](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/mcp-events), so AI agents can act the moment something happens: an email arrives, an issue is opened, a workflow fails. [Hookdeck Event Gateway](https://hookdeck.com) receives, verifies and delivers every event. For example, an email arrives at a Resend address, and ChatGPT, subscribed through the bridge, acts on it: ![ChatGPT, subscribed through the bridge, reporting "New inbound email" with the sender, the subject "Hello ChatGPT from the MCP Events bridge" and the recipient, under an "Inbound email alerts" task that is Monitoring](docs/images/chatgpt-email-event.png) ## Why MCP Events is an experimental MCP extension that lets an agent subscribe to events instead of polling for them, and ChatGPT supports it. But an agent can only subscribe to MCP servers that implement it, and almost none do yet, while nearly every service already sends webhooks. The bridge closes that gap: - **Webhooks become MCP Events.** Sources: Resend inbound email, GitHub, any of 163 Event Gateway source types (Stripe, Slack, Shopify and more), and webhooks from any HTTP sender, such as a service you've built, verified with HMAC, Standard Webhooks, Basic auth or an API key. Add others with `defineSource`. - **Subscribers choose what wakes them.** Events have filters, such as an email's sender, or a GitHub repository and action. - **Every event verified, delivered and recorded.** Event Gateway verifies each service's signatures, retries failed deliveries, drops duplicates within an hour, and keeps a record of every event and attempt. - **Stateless.** Each subscription is an Event Gateway connection, so there's no database. # Spring Boot Runtime Diagnostics MCP

[Chinese README](README.zh-CN.md)

Give your coding assistant read-only access to the runtime state of a local Spring Boot application. Eight MCP tools use authorized Actuator and OpenAPI data to diagnose issues such as missing beans, unregistered routes, and slow startup.

Listed in [Awesome MCP Servers (Developer Tools)](https://github.com/punkpeye/awesome-mcp-servers/pull/18153/files) · [View the tools on Glama](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/neilmorse/spring-runtime-mcp)

## What can it check?

| Your question | What it provides |
| --- | --- |
| Why was a Bean not created? | Beans, dependencies and condition reports, with blocking chains when evidence is sufficient |
| Is this route registered? | Actual paths, HTTP methods, Controllers and MVC/WebFlux mappings |
| What is unhealthy? | Visible components and liveness/readiness status |
| Did a migration fail? | Reported Flyway/Liquibase records, states and checksums |
| What made startup slow? | Slow steps and their parent chains |
| Where did a configuration value come from? | Sources for registered properties; configuration diagnostics require opt-in |
| Is this API in OpenAPI? | Operations, schemas and references within the document |
| Does the process match my expectations? | Compare the Bean, route, migration version and profile expectations you supply |

For example, ask: “Check whether GET /orders/{id} is registered and tell me which Controller handles it.” The server reads mapping metadata without calling the business endpoint.

## Get started

### Try the demo without a Spring Boot app

The [synthetic route demo](docs/demo.md) uses the public package and bundled data to show which controller handles a route. It runs without a Spring process or an MCP client.

### Connect an MCP client to your app

You need Python 3.11+, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and permission to read a local Spring Boot application's management endpoints. Confirm the endpoints and permissions in the [target setup guide](docs/target-app-setup.md). These commands use **0.2.12 Alpha**.


# Sealbridge

**English** | [日本語 (README.ja.md)](./README.ja.md)

Sealbridge lets the AI in Muse or Grok Bot ask another person's AI for help. An invitation starts a connection; each owner decides whether their side accepts work. DIDs identify peers; names are local shortcuts.

## Install on Muse

Paste `https://github.com/sealbridge/sealbridge` into Muse and say **「これ入れて」** (install this). Muse prepares Node.js and the other tools and installs from source. The invite/role features below are included in the prepared 0.9.0 release. Until npm 0.9.0 is published, install from GitHub main.

### Create an invitation (for example, on Muse)

Ask Muse to create an invite and keep its worker running. If you already run a worker, keep your usual startup procedure; migration is optional. To try it with commands:

```sh
sealbridge doctor
sealbridge config auto-accept invited write
sealbridge worker start --adapter sandbox --allow-local-pc --name Muse
```

Share the printed invitation link and keep the process running. This example explicitly allows invited tasks and uses a sandbox adapter that echoes JSON; its host declaration requires write permission even for an echo. For real work, configure your AI adapter and owner acceptance rule. `--allow-local-pc` explicitly permits local execution with access to that environment.

### Receive the invitation

Muse can import the link as an argument. Choose a name used only on your side:

```sh
sealbridge accept "https://sealbridge.app/i#acp-invite:..." --alias muse
sealbridge delegate --to muse --title "Quick check" --description "Read input and return JSON" --input '{"text":"hello"}' --auto-approve --audit audit.jsonl
sealbridge connections list
sealbridge audit-verify audit.jsonl
```

Import alone grants neither connection consent nor task permission. Explicit non-interactive CLI delegation to an invite peer is consent to connect. After verifying a signed ACCEPT from the matching invite DID, the importer records its connection too. Failure before reaching the peer, a DID mismatch, or `CONNECTION_TARGET_CONFLICT` records nothing. Use `--no-connect` for a one-off send. Recording prints an English/Japanese notice and a JSON `connectionRecorded` field; incoming work remains **off**. The TTY connection prompt and MCP `connect: true` form remain unchanged.

Connection recording is best-effort: a store failure does not abort accepted work. Bilingual stderr and JSON `connectionRecordWarning` with code `CONNECTION_RECORD_FAILED` advi

  send review. Every other client gets the same results as text.

no message bodies.

# 3DCraft

**3DCraft is an open-source parametric 3D CAD modeller built with and for AI: every action is a command, and every result is checked.**

*An agent builds. A machine checks. You decide.*

**[3dcraft.dev](https://3dcraft.dev/)**: the website, with the guide and the examples ·
**[Try it in your browser](https://3dcraft.dev/app/)** ·
**[Download](https://github.com/johancoppens/3dcraft/releases/latest)**

![The 3DCraft window with the spiral staircase example: its 93 features and 16 checks, all passing, in the side panel, the history player under them, the view cube and the display bar](docs/img/window.png)

## Three ways to use it

1. **Make models with AI.** Describe a part to an AI agent. It builds the part in the window you are watching,
   step by step; you point at a face, ask for a change, and check the result. Then export it for a 3D printer,
   a laser cutter, a mill or a workshop.
2. **Use a Jig.** A Jig is a finished design with a form: the sizes that matter are fields, the rest follows
   by formulas, and every result is checked. Take the sundial: choose your place, say whether it lies in the
   garden or hangs on a wall and which way that wall faces, and you get a brass dial to laser cut and engrave
   that reads the clock time where you live. No AI needed.
3. **Build your own application on it.** The engine is a Rust library, and every command is also reachable
   from the command line, a JSON control channel and an MCP server. A gear generator, a furniture
   configurator, a CAD interface with buttons: each can be a separate program on top of 3DCraft. The licence
   is MIT.

3DCraft has no toolbar of modelling buttons. You model through commands: an agent sends them, a Jig's form
sends them, or you write them yourself. The window is there to watch, to point and to check. Whoever wants a
classic interface with buttons can build one on top: it would send the same commands.

It is written in pure Rust, with its own B-rep kernel, constraint solver, tessellator and renderers: no
OpenCascade, no Parasolid, no third-party geometry of any kind. Licence: [MIT](LICENSE).

## How it started

3DCraft started as an experiment. The occasion was practical: designing a CNC machine, furniture and the
bodies and mechanisms of marionettes, with open software and the help of an AI agent. The open tools of today
did not get there. So the question was turned around: can AI agents write a CAD kernel themselves, if a
machine checks every result?

candidates.readme_excerpt:
# inference-optimisation An agent skill for **hill-climbing the speed of a local LLM server** on any hardware and any quantization. It covers: - single-user and concurrent decode - speculative decoding - prefill - KV cache size - startup time and time to first token It works under a memory cap, and every result has to survive a full-context stability check. It encodes how we actually got these speedups. It is not a list of flags. The workflow: 1. Compute the theoretical ceiling. 2. Change one thing at a time. 3. Measure against interleaved controls. 4. Log every result, including the failures. 5. Gate on long-context retrieval. 6. Qualify a clean, pinned build before publishing. It works with Claude Code and any agent that loads `SKILL.md`-style skills. Any model can also follow it from [`PROMPT.md`](PROMPT.md). ## What we've been able to accomplish Results from the hill-climbs this skill was distilled from. candidates.description: AG-UI: the Agent-User Interaction Protocol. Bring Agents into Frontend Applications.
candidates.readme_excerpt:
### The open protocol that connects any agent to any app. **[Docs](https://docs.ag-ui.com)** · **[Examples](https://dojo.ag-ui.com)** · **[Spec](https://docs.ag-ui.com/spec/1.0)** · **[Discord](https://discord.gg/Jd3FzfdJa8)**

**AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications.** Agents don't fit the request/response model. They stream tokens, call tools mid-response, update shared state, pause for a human, and spawn subagents, and every framework does it differently. AG-UI replaces that custom wiring with one bi-directional event stream: the agent emits typed events, and any client can render them, no matter which framework built the agent. The same agent can power a web app, a mobile app, a terminal, or Slack.
